facts.statement: Euhelopus was a large, four-legged herbivore.
facts.quote: It was a large quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Euhelopus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, a trait shared with brachiosaurids and titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Like sauropods such as brachiosaurids and titanosaurs, Euhelopus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs.

facts.statement: Unlike most sauropod fossils, Euhelopus preserves a relatively complete skull.
facts.quote: Unlike most sauropod specimens, it has a relatively complete skull.

facts.statement: Euhelopus had a 4-meter long neck made up of 17 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Euhelopus was a relatively long-necked sauropod, with a 4-meter neck composed of 17 cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: The presacral vertebrae of Euhelopus possessed a camellate pneumatic structure with many small air chambers, similar to titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The presacral vertebrae had a camellate pneumatic structure, made of many small pneumatic chambers, as is characteristic of titanosauriforms and some mamenchisaurids.

facts.statement: Pneumatic air chambers in Euhelopus extended into the ilium, a feature also found in many titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Pneumatic chambers even extended into the ilium, as occurs in many titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Euhelopus teeth were inclined forward, indicated by the enamel edge running toward the top and a front buttress positioned closer to the top.
facts.quote: The teeth are inclined to the front as proven by the edge of the enamel at the front of the tooth running more in the direction of the top and a front buttress also located more closely to the top.

facts.statement: The middle and posterior dorsal vertebrae of Euhelopus display a "K" configuration in their parapophyseal and diapophyseal laminae.
facts.quote: The middle and posterior dorsal parapophyseal and diapophyseal laminae are arranged in a "K" configuration.

facts.statement: Euhelopus was the first dinosaur scientifically investigated from China, first seen in 1913, rediscovered in 1922, excavated in 1923, and studied by T'an that same year.
facts.quote: This discovery was paleontologically significant because it represented the first dinosaur scientifically investigated from China: seen in 1913, rediscovered in 1922, excavated in 1923, and studied by T'an during the same year.

facts.statement: The original discovery of Euhelopus remains was made by Catholic priest Father R. Mertens in 1913.
facts.quote: The original discovery was by a Catholic priest, Father R. Mertens, in 1913.

facts.statement: The genus was originally named Helopus, meaning "Marsh Foot", by Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman in 1929.
facts.quote: It was originally described and named Helopus, meaning "Marsh Foot", by the Swedish paleontologist Carl Wiman in 1929, after the Greek ἕλος, helos, "swamp", and πούς, pous, "foot".

facts.statement: The dinosaur was renamed Euhelopus in 1956 by Alfred Sherwood Romer.
facts.quote: The sauropod dinosaur was therefore renamed Euhelopus (True marsh-foot) in 1956 by Alfred Sherwood Romer.

facts.statement: Specimen PMU 24705 serves as the holotype for the species Euhelopus zdanskyi.
facts.quote: Specimen PMU 24705 (formerly PMU R233) forms according to Wilson & Upchurch the holotype, descriptive basis, for the species Euhelopus zdanskyi.

facts.statement: The Euhelopus specimens are housed at the Paleontological Museum of Uppsala University in Sweden, where mounted skeletons have been displayed since the 1930s.
facts.quote: Both specimens are housed in the collection of the Paleontological Museum of Uppsala University, in Uppsala, Sweden, where the mounted skeletons are displayed since the 1930s.

facts.statement: Most studies suggest Euhelopus is closely related to titanosaurs rather than mamenchisaurids.
facts.quote: Most studies favor a close relationship between Euhelopus and titanosaurs, rather than mamenchisaurids.

facts.statement: Euhelopus was originally estimated to weigh between 15 and 20 tonnes and reach an adult length of 15 meters.
facts.quote: Since its original description, Euhelopus has often been considered a rather large sauropod. It has been thought to weigh about 15 - 20 t and attain an adult length of 15 m.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Euhelopus weighed 3.5 tonnes and measured 11 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated the weight at 3.5 t and the body length at 11 m.

facts.statement: Later studies estimated Euhelopus' mass at 5.9 tonnes by Benson et al. and 3.6 tonnes by Larramendi et al.
facts.quote: Benson et al. estimated its mass at 5.9 t, whereas Larramendi et al. estimated it at 3.6 t.

facts.statement: While Euhelopus is similar to Mamenchisaurus, its exact taxonomic affinities remain controversial.
facts.quote: Euhelopus was a long-necked sauropod similar to Mamenchisaurus, but its affinities are controversial.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes a partial skull, lower jaws, twenty-five presacral vertebrae, and a left thighbone.
facts.quote: Specimen PMU 24705 consists of a partial skeleton with skull and lower jaws comprising these bones: the rostral part of the left nasal; a partial right jugal; the tapered jugal process of the postorbital, partially excavated; the dorsal process of the right quadratojugal; the fragmented left pterygoid (another fragment might be the right splenial, but it is too fragile to be removed from its matrix), a series of twenty-five presacral vertebrae and the left thighbone.

facts.statement: John Stanton McIntosh classified Euhelopus within the family Camarasauridae in 1990.
facts.quote: In 1990, John Stanton McIntosh placed Euhelopus in the Camarasauridae.

facts.statement: The evolutionary relationships of Euhelopus are debated, with some studies linking it to Mamenchisaurus-like sauropods and others grouping it with titanosaurs in the clade Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic affinities of Euhelopus are controversial, and it has been variously interpreted as having close affinities to Mamenchisaurus-like taxa or as being grouped together with titanosaurs in the clade Somphospondyli.

facts.statement: Euhelopus is classified within the unranked clade Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: Euhelopus belongs to the family Euhelopodidae.
facts.quote: familia: Euhelopodidae

facts.statement: The genus Euhelopus was established by Romer in 1956.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Romer, 1956

facts.statement: The species E. zdanskyi was originally described by Wiman in 1929.
facts.quote: species_authority: Wiman, 1929

facts.statement: Euhelopus lived during the early Cretaceous period, approximately 129 to 113 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 129 a 113 millones de años, desde el Barremiense al Aptiense, en lo que hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The original discovery of Euhelopus fossils was made by Catholic priest R. Mertens in 1913.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento original fue realizado por un sacerdote católico, el padre R. Mertens, en 1913.

facts.statement: Otto Zdansky excavated two skeletons of Euhelopus in March 1923.
facts.quote: En marzo de 1923, el estudiante austriaco Otto Zdansky excavó dos esqueletos en sitios a unos tres kilómetros de distancia.

facts.statement: The genus was originally named Helopus in 1929, derived from Greek words meaning "marsh foot".
facts.quote: El género fue inicialmente nombrado como Helopus en griego ἕλος, helos, "pantano" y πούς, pous, "pie". "pata del pantano" en 1929.

facts.statement: The name Helopus was changed to Euhelopus in 1956 by Romer because Helopus was already used for a bird species.
facts.quote: Pero este nombre, sin embargo, ya pertenecía a un ave porque el charrán del Caspio había sido nombrado Helopus caspius por Wagler en 1832, por lo que sería renombrado como Euhelopus que le antepuso el vocablo en griego eu significando verdadero pie de pantano en 1956 por Romer.

facts.statement: The type material of Euhelopus was excavated from the Mengyin Formation in Shandong Province, China.
facts.quote: El material tipo de Euhelopus fue excavado en la formación Mengyin en la provincia de Shandong, China.

facts.statement: Euhelopus was a large sauropod that reached lengths of 15 meters and weighed 20 tons.
facts.quote: El Euhelopus fue un gran saurópodo que llegó a medir 15 metros de largo y a pesar 20 toneladas.

facts.statement: Euhelopus had a long neck approximately 5 meters long with 19 vertebrae.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuello largo de alrededor de 5 metros, con 19 vértebras.

facts.statement: Euhelopus had a short, wide head with nostrils on top and a mouth full of pencil-like teeth that occupied the entire oral cavity, unlike Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Además poseía una cabeza corta y ancha con las fosas nasales en la parte superior y una boca repleta de dientes como lápices, juntos entre sí, y que ocupaban toda la cavidad oral y no solo en el hocico, como era el caso del Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Euhelopus had front legs slightly longer than its hind legs and a back that curved downward.
facts.quote: Sus patas delanteras eran algo más largas que las traseras y su lomo se curvaba hacia abajo.

facts.statement: The vertebrae of Euhelopus had hollow chambers similar to those of Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: Sus vértebras tenían cámaras huecas similares a la del Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: Euhelopus teeth were inclined forward, indicated by the enamel edge running more toward the top and a frontal ridge closer to the top.
facts.quote: Los dientes están inclinados hacia el frente, como lo demuestra el borde del esmalte en la parte delantera del diente que corre más en la dirección de la parte superior y un contrafuerte frontal también se encuentra más cerca de la parte superior.

facts.statement: The axis vertebra of Euhelopus had a hollow in the back of its neural canal with three deeper pneumatic depressions.
facts.quote: El axis, la segunda vértebra del cuello, tiene un hueco en la parte posterior de su canal neural, con tres depresiones neumáticas más profundas.

facts.statement: Postaxial cervical vertebrae in Euhelopus had variably developed epipophyses and subtler preepipophyses below the prezygapophyses.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales postaxiales, las vértebras del cuello detrás del axis, tienen epipófisis desarrolladas de manera variable y preepipopófisis más sutiles debajo de las prezigapófisis , proyecciones en el frente de la cresta entre la prezigapófisis y el cuerpo vertebral.

facts.statement: In Euhelopus neck vertebrae, pleurocoels were reduced to small holes.
facts.quote: En las vértebras del cuello, los pleurocoelos se reducen a agujeros, aberturas más pequeñas.

facts.statement: Mid-presacral neural spines in Euhelopus split or bifurcated, and anterior dorsal vertebrae had a median tubercle as large as the metapophyses, resulting in a "timid" condition.
facts.quote: Las espinas neurales presacras medias, de la parte posterior del cuello y la parte posterior de la espalda, se dividen o se bifurcan, y en la base del cuello y las vértebras dorsales anteriores tienen un tubérculo mediano que es al menos tan grande como los metapófisis, las puntas de la horquilla, lo que resulta en una condición "tímida".

facts.statement: Presacral pneumaticity in Euhelopus extended to the ilium, which was therefore permeated by air chambers.
facts.quote: La neumaticidad presacra se extiende hacia el ilion , que por lo tanto es permeada por cámaras de aire.

facts.statement: The Mengyin Formation dates from the Berriasian to the Valanginian stages.
facts.quote: La formación Mengyin se remonta desde Berriasiano al Valanginiano.

facts.statement: The Mengyin Formation was previously thought to have been deposited during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 129 to 113 million years ago.
facts.quote: Anteriormente, se consideraba que se había depositado durante las etapas del Barremiano al Aptiano del Cretácico, hace unos 129 a 113 millones de años.

facts.statement: Fossils of Euhelopus are housed in the Paleontological Museum at Uppsala University, Sweden.
facts.quote: Los fósiles se encuentran en el Museo de Paleontología de la Universidad de Uppsala, Suecia.

facts.statement: In 1929, Wiman was uncertain about the affinities of Helopus and placed it in its own family, Helopodidae.
facts.quote: Wiman en 1929 no estaba seguro de las afinidades de Helopus y lo colocó en una familia propia Helopodidae.

facts.statement: In 1956, Romer created the subfamily Euhelopodinae to include the animal.
facts.quote: Romer en 1956 creó Euhelopodinae para incluirlo.

facts.statement: In 1990, John Stanton McIntosh classified Euhelopus within the family Camarasauridae.
facts.quote: En 1990, John Stanton McIntosh colocó a Euhelopus en Camarasauridae.

facts.statement: Euhelopus shows phylogenetic affinity to the taxon Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Euhelopus demuestra afinidad filogenética al taxón Titanosauria.

facts.statement: It is unclear whether the family Euhelopodidae is monophyletic.
facts.quote: No está claro si los Euhelopodidae es monofiléticos.

facts.statement: Traditional claims that Euhelopus, Omeisaurus, Mamenchisaurus, and Shunosaurus form the monophyletic family Euhelopodidae are not supported by new phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: Las afirmaciones tradicionales de que Euhelopus , Omeisaurus, Mamenchisaurus y Shunosaurus forman la familia monofilética "Euhelopodidae" no están respaldadas por un nuevo análisis filogenético.

facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.quote: Family: Euhelopodidae
